task_name: Milepost Driving Academy - Scenario clip training library
client_brief:
Milepost is starting with two scenarios rather than the whole library. If these two land with learners and with the parents watching over their shoulder, we will commission the rest on the same pattern.

Our learners watch on a phone with the sound off, so nothing is spoken in these clips. No narration, no voice over, no synthetic instructor. The instruction goes on screen, word for word from the approved copy, one step at a time, in the order the copy gives, and the clips run silent.

Deliverables
1. Right turns explainer: 1 named export, 1920 by 1080, 12 to 15 seconds, silent. All five steps from the Right turns row on screen in order, then the callout for that row.
2. Four-way stops explainer: 1 named export, 1920 by 1080, 10 to 12 seconds, silent. All four steps from the Four-way stops row on screen in order, then the callout for that row.
3. Vertical lane changes example: 1 named export, 1080 by 1920, 6 to 9 seconds, silent. The scenario title and the callout only, so we can see how the road reads upright on a phone before we commit the rest of the library to that format.

Show the manoeuvre, do not imply it. A learner should be able to see the car do the thing the step describes. If a step is not visible in the footage we have given you, say so in the delivery manifest rather than cutting unrelated road shots together until the manoeuvre looks finished.

Two notes on the source. The two four way stop takes are the same junction filmed on two passes in different lanes, so please do not present them as two different junctions. Road context has to stay readable in the upright example: if the lane line leaves the frame, the example teaches nothing.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.
Video delivery means a playable MP4, not a storyboard, a still montage PDF or an editing log. Audio expectations are stated on each film. No film in this commission carries speech or music: every clip is delivered silent, with the instruction set on screen.
Authored animation can exceed the duration of still source images. Live action edits require adequate distinct footage; looping a short clip is not a substitute for missing coverage.
Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.sector: Driver education and road safety training (accredited in car and classroom academy)
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Established 2009 in Burlington, Vermont. Small: two instructors, roughly sixty learners a term.
brand_identity.about: Milepost is an accredited driving academy in Vermont running in car lessons and a classroom course. Two instructors, about sixty learners a term, mostly sixteen to nineteen with a steady number of adult beginners. Our reputation is that we are calm and thorough, and every learner leaves certain about what they are looking at. Everything we make has to earn the trust of a nervous learner and the parent paying for the course.
brand_identity.audience: Learners sixteen to nineteen plus adult beginners, with the purchase decision usually made by a parent. People who want reassurance that the school is careful and legitimate.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Mid, accredited and dependable. Sixty dollars an hour. Not a budget app, not a premium driving experience brand.
brand_identity.typography: Display is Baskerville Display PT, Bold for the school name, Regular for scenario titles, nothing else. What a viewer notices first is the scenario number set in Baskerville Display PT at three times the title size, in Signal Green, with a 3 px Caution Amber rule beneath. Inter Regular and Semibold, tabular lining figures throughout, carries every step, callout and caption. Step title 72 px, step body 44 px on 58 px leading, callout 56 px, caption 32 px, vertical title 64 px, printed guide 11 pt on 16 pt. Never set a step in italic or caps.
brand_identity.voice: Calm, instructive, reassuring. One idea at a time, numbered where it helps, no slang and no drama. Speaks plainly to a beginner and to the parent reading over their shoulder.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: Everything a learner currently sees from us dates to 2019 and looks it. The printer holds the press file for the guide, but the source files for our simplified sign shapes are gone: they only survive as a photograph of a sheet our first designer printed and taped to the wall, so those glyphs have to be recovered from that. No brand typeface was ever locked, so the type system is open for you to set to our legibility standard.
brand_identity.values: Certainty over style. A learner and a parent must always be sure what they are looking at. Nothing stylised, nothing that reads as styling over substance, consistency that shows the school is careful.
brand_identity.signature_type_move: Every scenario carries its number set in Baskerville Display PT at three times the title size, in Signal Green, with a 3 px Caution Amber rule directly beneath it.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Treat measured file duration and stream metadata as authoritative. Do not infer spoken content from silent clips or use a visual summary as a transcript.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.
source_of_truth: Approved client notes and permissions govern factual corrections. V4 output register governs commissioned output classes and sizes. Original rows are not automatically approved copy.

deliverables.name: Right turns explainer

values.Steps: 1. Slow down early and get into the correct position. 2. Signal right in good time. 3. Check your mirrors and the road you are turning into. 4. Take the turn at a speed that lets you stay in your own lane. 5. Straighten up and build speed gently once you are round.

raw_values.Steps: 1. Slow down early and get into the correct position. 2. Signal right in good time. 3. Check your mirrors and the road you are turning into. 4. Take the turn at a speed that lets you stay in your own lane. 5. Straighten up and build speed gently once you are round.

deliverables.required_content: The scenario title “Right turns”, then the five approved steps on screen in order, “Slow down early and get into the correct position”, “Signal right in good time”, “Check your mirrors and the road you are turning into”, “Take the turn at a speed that lets you stay in your own lane” and “Straighten up and build speed gently once you are round”, closing on the callout “Slow in, steady out.”, over footage of a car completing a right turn.
acceptance_requirements: The narration matches the visual scenario.
The instruction agrees with the cleared training copy.
expert_review_criteria: The finishing looks polished at the delivered size.
The visual character feels like Milepost Driving Academy.
The intended visual focus is clear throughout the sequence.
The creative treatment suits the audience described in the brand brief.
The composition feels native to its stated delivery format.
deliverables.record_field_policy: The approved_values in source_record are the scoring target. raw_values are retained only for provenance and may contain known export defects.

deliverables.name: Four-way stops explainer

values.Steps: 1. Come to a full stop at the line, every time. 2. The first vehicle to stop is the first to go. 3. If two of you arrive together, the one on the right goes first. 4. When it is your turn, move off clearly so others know.
values.Callout: Full stop, then first come, first go.
